pretreatments.description: Microwave pretreatment (MP) involving irradiation with an electromagnetic field at 900 W and 2450 MHz, with varying treatment times from 1 to 60 minutes, and different microwave power levels from 90 W to 720 W. The substrate was placed in a polytetra fluoro ethylene sealed container with a 1:50 ratio of GMM to water. This process aimed to enhance the substrate lysis rate and increase biomethane yields.

Surfactant microwave pretreatment (SMP) combining microwave pretreatment with the addition of sodium dodecylbenzene sulfonate (SDBS) as a surface active medium. The SDBS concentration ranged from 0.005 to 0.5 g/g TS, at an optimal MP conditions. The substrate was also placed in a polytetra fluoro ethylene sealed container with a 1:50 ratio of GMM to water. This treatment was performed at a fixed microwave power and treatment time, and was used to decrease the energy demand of microwave pretreatment and to achieve greater liquefaction for increased biomethane yield.

Hydrolysis and acidogenesis study involving the use of sludge from an anaerobic digester as inoculum. The pretreated samples (MP and SMP) and the inoculum were placed in bottles at a 9:1 proportion, thermally treated at 102 °C for 30 minutes, and then treated with 2-bromoethyl sulfonic acid (BESA) to eliminate oxygen. The samples were then incubated at 35 °C with orbital shaking at 110 rpm for 72 hours.

Biochemical methane potential (BMP) study utilizing rumen fluid as inoculum and GMM samples. The BMP study was conducted in 2L bottles with a 3:1 ratio of rumen fluid to GMM samples, incubated at 35 °C with orbital shaking at 110 rpm. The biogas content was measured using gas chromatography with a thermal conductivity detector and porapak Q column.
